**International Copper Study Group Environmental and Economic Committee Twenty Seventh Regular Meeting 6 October 2009, 10:45 a.m. – 1.00 p.m. Lisbon, Portugal** **ICSG/EEC27/4** # **Study on End Use** ## **1) Background** ## **a) End Use and ICSG** Given the ICSG mandate to increase copper market transparency and the relatively low level of publicly available information about copper end use, it is logical that ICSG member government representatives and industry advisors have expressed interest in ICSG conducting research on this vital final link in the supply chain over the years. Since as early as 1994, when the Statistical Committee Ad Hoc Group on End Uses met at the ICA offices in New York City, ICSG has discussed possible ways to gather and report on the consumption of copper in end use products. Among the difficulties encountered in conducting work related to end use have been: - The lack of available and detailed data - Confidentiality issues not only at the firm level but also at the industry associations - Difficulties associated with the lack of uniformity in end use categories and comparability of end use data and - Lack of responsiveness to ICSG surveys. In 1995-1996 a concerted effort was made to harmonize end use statistics reported by the Copper Development Association and the International Wrought Copper Council and to distribute end use surveys to ICSG member countries. Data was collected for selected countries for the years 1990, 1993 and 1994, although lack of responsiveness to ICSG surveys remained an issue and data gaps persisted. While the end use issue was revisited again in 1998 in the Statistics Committee when it was suggested that industry could be surveyed directly, ICSG work on end use has not progressed much since then in part due to the above mentioned difficulties but also due in part to ICSG members having given higher priority to other ongoing items on the ICSG work program. (The secretariat’s potential collaboration in a new end use study would also be without prejudice to the ongoing approved regular work items and projects.) ## **b) End Use and Other Organizations** Industry associations such as the International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC), Copper Development Association (CDA) and International Copper Association (ICA) have continued to attempt to collect end use data in recent years with varying degrees of success. Since 2007 ICA has produced, on an annual basis, an end use data set accounting for all copper use globally. This data shows copper use in a matrix, the cells of which are defined by: 

- End use sector and application (e.g. Building Construction, Water distribution), 

- Product (e.g. copper tube) 

- Main World region (e.g. N. America, China, W. Europe)

However, the compilation of a complete and verifiable data set for end use has remained a difficult task to accomplish. As a result of the problems associated with the lack of coverage depth and independent verification, ICA representatives expressed an interest in collaborating with ICSG on improving end use statistics. Discussions with ICA have identified the following advantages of collaborating on end use: 

- ICSG has a strong, global reputation and considerable in-house experience in the field of data provision, which is central to its mandate. In contrast ICA is recognized as, and intends to remain, the prime organization for developing and defending copper markets. 

- ICSG can most likely obtain greater exposure for the data via its press releases and recognized data provision role, so increasing the overall usefulness of the effort, and in turn ICSG, to industry. 

- On the analysis side, ICSG, as a government organization in support of the industry, will have greater scope to process the data, including the possibility of governmentreviewed demand projections. In contrast, ICA and its members are committed to full compliance with antitrust rules and cannot and will not project future demand. 

## **2) Recent Developments in the Project Proposal** 

At the April 2009 Statistical Committee meeting, the secretariat advised members that it could re-examine the end use data project currently listed on the Work Program but which had been put on hold. The secretariat further advised members that due to the complexity involved with the end use issue, it might be best to first evaluate how best to proceed with the work, potentially in conjunction with other organizations such as ICA, before launching a new project. 

Following the April 2009 ICSG meetings, secretariat staff held discussions with ICA at which time ICA confirmed their interest in collaborating with ICSG on end use; specifically, transferring the management responsibility and some resources to ICSG. 

Secretariat staff indicated that more detailed information about ICA methodology, costs, etc. would be necessary before discussions could move forward. ICA subsequently provided the secretariat with more detailed information about their methodology. The basic ICA method for producing this data is as follows: 

- ICA management commissions a consultant to produce a ‘straw man’ data set, drawing 

- on all their third-party reports, and using further market in

telligence 

- ICA Management distributes this information to other organizations for comment 

- ICA Management collects and processes comments and amendments 

- ICA Management publishes final data set with basic analysis 

In addition, ICA forwarded a sample of the data collected and responded to a series of secretariat questions. The secretariat and ICA staff held a follow-up teleconference in July 2009 to clarify some important outstanding issues including confidentiality of data, participation of ICA network members, subcontractors and other organizations. 

Should the collaboration go ahead, it is expected that ICSG would take over the ICA Management role described above, and that ICSG will look for other potential ways to conduct this work as ICSG knowledge and experience in the field grows. In this way, an increasingly accurate and sophisticated output will be achieved. 

3 

## **3) Current Status** 

ICA is currently in discussions with those organizations that have provided data verification and comments in the past in order to ensure that there would be no deterioration in participation levels or quality of data management in a collaborative effort between ICA and ICSG. 

Dependent on the outcome of these discussions (there are several specific concerns to be addressed), the secretariat will submit a proposal for an end use project to ICSG members at the October 2009 ICSG meeting.
